description: Task 3.2 VS Code Extension. Author a new xplainit-vscode/ TypeScript extension providing inline hover explanations, step-through visualization, an error analysis panel, and trace recording/playback, backed by the JSON trace format that xplainit-core emits and the CLI reads. SANDBOX CONSTRAINT: node/npm are absent and the VS Code marketplace/vsce is unreachable (INTEGRATIONS_ONLY), so `npm install`, TypeScript compilation via tsc, and `vsce package` CANNOT run here. Author the source honestly and completely; document the build/package/run steps as blocked-in-sandbox rather than claiming they pass.
steps: Create the xplainit-vscode/ directory with the structure from the plan: package.json (extension manifest: name, engines.vscode, contributes.commands for record/playback/explain, activationEvents), tsconfig.json, and src/extension.ts, src/traceProvider.ts, src/explanationHover.ts, src/errorPanel.ts, plus syntaxes/xplainit-trace.json.

extension.ts: register the extension activate()/deactivate(), the commands (e.g. xplainit.recordTrace, xplainit.playbackTrace, xplainit.explainFunction), and register the hover provider and error panel. Use the @types/vscode API surface as documented (write against the standard vscode module even though it cannot be npm-installed here).

explanationHover.ts: implement a HoverProvider that, given a loaded trace JSON (same ExecutionEvent shape produced by xplainit-core, fields: event_type/id/timestamp/location{file,line,column}/name/etc.), returns a hover Markdown string explaining what happened at the hovered file:line. Match trace events by SourceLocation file+line.

traceProvider.ts: load a trace JSON file, index events by location and by task/function, and drive step-through visualization (a TreeDataProvider or webview timeline). Include record/playback: 'record' shells out to the xplainit CLI (from FEAT-001) to produce a trace JSON; 'playback' steps through the loaded events highlighting the corresponding source lines.

errorPanel.ts: a webview panel that lists error events from the trace (is_error semantics: exception/runtime_error/type_error/null_pointer_error/index_out_of_bounds/division_by_zero/stack_overflow/panic/etc.) with the ErrorExplainer-style analysis text, ideally by invoking `xplainit analyze` on the trace and rendering its output.
syntaxes/xplainit-trace.json: a TextMate grammar so .xplainit-trace / trace JSON files get basic syntax highlighting.

Add xplainit-vscode/README.md documenting: what the extension does; the EXACT build/run/package commands (npm install; npm run compile / tsc; F5 to launch Extension Development Host; vsce package); and an explicit 'Sandbox status' section stating these commands could not be executed here because node/npm and vsce are unavailable under INTEGRATIONS_ONLY, so the TypeScript is authored but not compiled/packaged in this environment. Do not claim a build or test passed.
Add a .gitignore entry for xplainit-vscode/node_modules and out/ (do not commit installed deps).

Sanity-check the TypeScript by hand for obvious type/consistency errors against the documented vscode API (there is no compiler available). Ensure the extension does not affect the Rust workspace build.
acceptance_criteria: xplainit-vscode/ exists with package.json, tsconfig.json, src/extension.ts, src/traceProvider.ts, src/explanationHover.ts, src/errorPanel.ts, and syntaxes/xplainit-trace.json.
The extension source consumes the same JSON trace shape emitted by xplainit-core / the xplainit CLI (consistent field names).
README.md documents build/package steps AND explicitly records that npm/tsc/vsce could not be run in this sandbox (honest blocked status), with no false claim of a successful build.
The Rust workspace still builds and tests green (the new directory does not break cargo).
verification: cargo build --release  (confirm the new non-Rust directory does not affect the workspace)
ls xplainit-vscode/src and confirm all named source files exist

Document (do not fake) that `npm install` / `tsc` / `vsce package` are unavailable in this sandbox; if a JS toolchain were present the reviewer/next environment runs `npm install && npm run compile` in xplainit-vscode/.
findings: Authored the standalone xplainit-vscode/ TypeScript extension (NOT added to the Cargo workspace; root Cargo.toml untouched). Files: package.json (manifest with engines.vscode ^1.85.0, activationEvents, contributes.commands for loadTrace/recordTrace/playbackTrace/stepForward/stepBackward/stopPlayback/goToEvent/explainFunction/showErrorPanel, configuration keys xplainit.cliPath and xplainit.recordCommand, xplainitTimeline tree view, xplainit-trace language + grammar), tsconfig.json (strict, commonjs, ES2020, out/), src/trace.ts (shared data model), src/traceProvider.ts (TraceProvider), src/explanationHover.ts (HoverProvider), src/errorPanel.ts (webview), src/extension.ts (activate/deactivate + registrations), syntaxes/xplainit-trace.json (TextMate grammar), language-configuration.json, .vscode/launch.json (F5 Run Extension), .gitignore, README.md. TRACE-SHAPE DECISIONS: verified against xplainit-core/src/events.rs and the FEAT-001 CLI analyze.rs test fixtures. ExecutionEvent uses serde's default EXTERNALLY-TAGGED representation, so each event serializes as a single-key object keyed by the variant name (e.g. {"FunctionEnter":{...}}, {"DivisionByZero":{...}}), NOT the snake_case event_type() string. The Value enum is also externally tagged (e.g. {"Integer":10}, {"String":"hi"}) with unit variant Null serializing as bare "Null". trace.ts models EventVariant as the 21 variant names, keeps EVENT_TYPE_BY_VARIANT (function_enter, division_by_zero, etc.) and ERROR_VARIANTS in sync with events.rs (is_error() set: Exception/SyntaxError/RuntimeError/TypeError/NullPointerError/IndexOutOfBounds/DivisionByZero/StackOverflow/Panic/InfiniteLoopDetected/DeadlockDetected/MemoryLeakDetected), matches events by SourceLocation{file,line} (with basename fallback), and formatValue() decodes the tagged Value shape. record shells out to `<cliPath> <recordCommand> <target>` (default `xplainit run`, piping stdout to the trace file); the error panel and report use `xplainit analyze <trace>` and `xplainit report <trace> --format <fmt>`, consistent with FEAT-001 subcommands. VERIFICATION DONE: cargo build --release and cargo test both green; the new non-Rust directory does not affect the workspace. BLOCKED-IN-SANDBOX (documented, not a feature failure): npm install, npm run compile / tsc, F5 Extension Development Host, and vsce package could NOT be executed here because node/npm are absent and the npm registry + VS Code marketplace/vsce are unreachable under INTEGRATIONS_ONLY. The README.md 'Sandbox status' section states this explicitly and gives the exact commands to run in a Node-enabled environment. The TypeScript was hand-checked for type/API consistency against the documented vscode API; a real tsc type-check should be run where a JS toolchain exists. No build/test success was fabricated.
